quotes.sourceExcerpt: 學而時習之，不亦說乎？
quotes.textChinese: 学习后常常温习，不也令人喜悦吗？
quotes.textEnglish: Is it not a pleasure to learn and then practise what you have learned?

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 有朋自遠方來，不亦樂乎？
quotes.textChinese: 有志同道合的朋友远道而来，不也快乐吗？
quotes.textEnglish: Is it not a joy to have friends come from afar?

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 吾日三省吾身：為人謀而不忠乎？與朋友交而不信乎？傳不習乎？
quotes.textChinese: 我每天多次反省自己：替人谋事是否尽心？与朋友交往是否守信？所学是否温习？
quotes.textEnglish: Each day I examine myself: have I been faithful in serving others, trustworthy with friends, and diligent in what I have learned?

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 過則勿憚改。
quotes.textChinese: 有了过错，就不要怕改正。
quotes.textEnglish: When you make a mistake, do not be afraid to correct it.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 不患人之不己知，患不知人也。
quotes.textChinese: 不怕别人不了解自己，只担心自己不了解别人。
quotes.textEnglish: Do not worry that others fail to know you; worry that you fail to know others.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 溫故而知新，可以為師矣。
quotes.textChinese: 温习旧知而能有新体会，便可以为师。
quotes.textEnglish: Review the old and discover the new; then you may teach others.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 學而不思則罔，思而不學則殆。
quotes.textChinese: 只学不思会迷惘，只思不学会危殆。
quotes.textEnglish: Learning without thought leads to confusion; thought without learning leads to danger.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 知之為知之，不知為不知，是知也。
quotes.textChinese: 知道就是知道，不知道就是不知道，这才是真正的明智。
quotes.textEnglish: To know what you know and know what you do not know is true knowledge.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 見賢思齊焉，見不賢而內自省也。
quotes.textChinese: 看见贤者，就想着向他看齐；看见不贤的人，就反省自己。
quotes.textEnglish: When you see someone worthy, think how to become their equal; when you see the unworthy, examine yourself.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 敏而好學，不恥下問。
quotes.textChinese: 聪敏好学，向不如自己的人请教也不以为耻。
quotes.textEnglish: Be eager to learn and never ashamed to ask those below you.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 知者樂水，仁者樂山。
quotes.textChinese: 智者乐于水，仁者乐于山。
quotes.textEnglish: The wise delight in water; the humane delight in mountains.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 不憤不啟，不悱不發。
quotes.textChinese: 不到努力求解时，不去启发；不到想说却说不出时，不去开导。
quotes.textEnglish: I do not enlighten those who are not eager to learn, nor help those who are not striving to express themselves.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 三人行，必有我師焉。
quotes.textChinese: 几个人同行，其中必定有人可以做我的老师。
quotes.textEnglish: When walking with two others, I can learn from each of them.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。
quotes.textChinese: 读书人不可不志向广大、意志坚毅，因为责任重大，道路长远。
quotes.textEnglish: A scholar must be broad-minded and resolute, for the burden is heavy and the road is long.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 譬如為山，未成一簣，止，吾止也。
quotes.textChinese: 好比堆山，只差一筐土却停下来，那是我自己停下的。
quotes.textEnglish: Like building a mountain: if you stop one basket short, you have stopped yourself.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 覆一簣、進、吾往也。
quotes.textChinese: 好比填平地面，哪怕只倒下一筐土，继续前进也是我自己在走。
quotes.textEnglish: Like filling a hollow: even one basket forward is your own progress.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 君子成人之美，不成人之惡。
quotes.textChinese: 君子成全别人的好事，不促成别人的坏事。
quotes.textEnglish: The noble person helps others achieve what is good, not what is bad.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 君子以文會友，以友輔仁。
quotes.textChinese: 君子以学问结交朋友，以朋友辅助仁德。
quotes.textEnglish: The noble person meets friends through learning and grows in goodness through friendship.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 知者不惑，仁者不憂，勇者不懼。
quotes.textChinese: 有智慧的人不迷惑，仁德的人不忧愁，勇敢的人不畏惧。
quotes.textEnglish: The wise are free from doubt, the humane from worry, and the brave from fear.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: 性相近也，習相遠也。
quotes.textChinese: 人的本性相近，后天习染使彼此渐远。
quotes.textEnglish: People are close in nature; habit carries them far apart.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Heaven is long-enduring and earth continues long.
quotes.textChinese: 天地所以能长久，是因为它们不为自己而生。
quotes.textEnglish: Heaven is long-enduring and earth continues long.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: The highest excellence is like (that of) water.
quotes.textChinese: 最高的善，像水一样。
quotes.textEnglish: The highest excellence is like (that of) water.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: its occupying, without striving (to the contrary), the low place which all men dislike.
quotes.textChinese: 水善于滋养万物，却安居于众人不喜欢的低处。
quotes.textEnglish: its occupying, without striving (to the contrary), the low place which all men dislike.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: It is better to leave a vessel unfilled, than to attempt to carry it when it is full.
quotes.textChinese: 器皿留有余地，胜过装满后勉强承载。
quotes.textEnglish: It is better to leave a vessel unfilled, than to attempt to carry it when it is full.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: When the work is done, and one's name is becoming distinguished, to withdraw into obscurity is the way of Heaven.
quotes.textChinese: 功成名就之后退居幕后，才合乎天道。
quotes.textEnglish: When the work is done, and one's name is becoming distinguished, to withdraw into obscurity is the way of Heaven.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: The partial becomes complete; the crooked, straight; the empty, full; the worn out, new.
quotes.textChinese: 委曲反能保全，弯曲反能伸直，空虚反能充实，陈旧反能更新。
quotes.textEnglish: The partial becomes complete; the crooked, straight; the empty, full; the worn out, new.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: He is free from self-display, and therefore he shines; from self-assertion, and therefore he is distinguished.
quotes.textChinese: 不自我表现，所以光彩；不自我夸耀，所以显明。
quotes.textEnglish: He is free from self-display, and therefore he shines; from self-assertion, and therefore he is distinguished.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: A violent wind does not last for a whole morning; a sudden rain does not last for the whole day.
quotes.textChinese: 狂风不会吹一早上，暴雨不会下一整天。
quotes.textEnglish: A violent wind does not last for a whole morning; a sudden rain does not last for the whole day.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: He who stands on his tiptoes does not stand firm.
quotes.textChinese: 踮起脚的人站不稳。
quotes.textEnglish: He who stands on his tiptoes does not stand firm.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Man takes his law from the Earth; the Earth takes its law from Heaven; Heaven takes its law from the Tao.
quotes.textChinese: 人取法于地，地取法于天，天取法于道。
quotes.textEnglish: Man takes his law from the Earth; the Earth takes its law from Heaven; Heaven takes its law from the Tao.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Gravity is the root of lightness; stillness, the ruler of movement.
quotes.textChinese: 沉稳是轻率的根，宁静是躁动的主。
quotes.textEnglish: Gravity is the root of lightness; stillness, the ruler of movement.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: The skilful traveller leaves no traces of his wheels or footsteps.
quotes.textChinese: 善于行走的人，不留下车辙和脚印。
quotes.textEnglish: The skilful traveller leaves no traces of his wheels or footsteps.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: He who knows other men is discerning; he who knows himself is intelligent.
quotes.textChinese: 了解别人是明智，了解自己才是真正聪明。
quotes.textEnglish: He who knows other men is discerning; he who knows himself is intelligent.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: He who overcomes others is strong; he who overcomes himself is mighty.
quotes.textChinese: 胜过别人算有力量，胜过自己才是真强大。
quotes.textEnglish: He who overcomes others is strong; he who overcomes himself is mighty.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: When its work is accomplished, it does not claim the name of having done it.
quotes.textChinese: 万物成就之后，道不居功。
quotes.textEnglish: When its work is accomplished, it does not claim the name of having done it.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: The soft overcomes the hard; and the weak the strong.
quotes.textChinese: 柔弱胜刚强。
quotes.textEnglish: The soft overcomes the hard; and the weak the strong.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: The Tao in its regular course does nothing (for the sake of doing it), and so there is nothing which it does not do.
quotes.textChinese: 道常无为，却没有什么不成就。
quotes.textEnglish: The Tao in its regular course does nothing (for the sake of doing it), and so there is nothing which it does not do.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: The softest thing in the world dashes against and overcomes the hardest.
quotes.textChinese: 天下最柔软的东西，能穿透天下最坚硬的东西。
quotes.textEnglish: The softest thing in the world dashes against and overcomes the hardest.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: The tree which fills the arms grew from the tiniest sprout.
quotes.textChinese: 合抱的大树，生于细小的萌芽。
quotes.textEnglish: The tree which fills the arms grew from the tiniest sprout.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: The journey of a thousand li commenced with a single step.
quotes.textChinese: 千里之行，始于足下。
quotes.textEnglish: The journey of a thousand li commenced with a single step.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Of my grandfather Verus I have learned to be gentle and meek, and to refrain from all anger and passion.
quotes.textChinese: 我从祖父维鲁斯那里学会温和谦逊，克制怒气与激情。
quotes.textEnglish: Of my grandfather Verus I have learned to be gentle and meek, and to refrain from all anger and passion.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: To Rusticus I am beholding, that I first entered into the conceit that my life wanted some redress and cure.
quotes.textChinese: 我感念鲁斯提库斯，让我初次明白自己需要修正与疗治。
quotes.textEnglish: To Rusticus I am beholding, that I first entered into the conceit that my life wanted some redress and cure.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: From Apollonius, true liberty, and unvariable steadfastness, and not to regard anything at all, though never so little, but right and reason.
quotes.textChinese: 我从阿波罗尼乌斯学到真正的自由、坚定不移，以及凡事以正当与理性为准。
quotes.textEnglish: From Apollonius, true liberty, and unvariable steadfastness, and not to regard anything at all, though never so little, but right and reason.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Of Sextus, mildness and the pattern of a family governed with paternal affection;
quotes.textChinese: 我从塞克斯图斯学到温和，以及以亲情治理家庭的典范。
quotes.textEnglish: Of Sextus, mildness and the pattern of a family governed with paternal affection;

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Of Catulus, not to contemn any friend's expostulation, though unjust, but to strive to reduce him to his former disposition.
quotes.textChinese: 我从卡图卢斯学到，即使朋友的劝告未必公允，也要努力使彼此重归和好。
quotes.textEnglish: Of Catulus, not to contemn any friend's expostulation, though unjust, but to strive to reduce him to his former disposition.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: From my brother Severus, to be kind and loving to all them of my house and family;
quotes.textChinese: 我从兄长塞维鲁斯学到，善待并关爱家人。
quotes.textEnglish: From my brother Severus, to be kind and loving to all them of my house and family;

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Betimes in the morning say to thyself, This day I shalt have to do with an idle curious man,
quotes.textChinese: 清晨先提醒自己：今天可能会遇见懒散而挑剔的人。
quotes.textEnglish: Betimes in the morning say to thyself, This day I shalt have to do with an idle curious man,

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Let it be thy earnest and incessant care
quotes.textChinese: 把认真做好眼前之事，当作持续不断的责任。
quotes.textEnglish: Let it be thy earnest and incessant care

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Consider how quickly all things are dissolved and resolved.
quotes.textChinese: 想想万物消散、复归原状是多么迅速。
quotes.textEnglish: Consider how quickly all things are dissolved and resolved.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Let nothing be done rashly, and at random, but all things according to the most exact and perfect rules of art.
quotes.textChinese: 不要草率行事或随意而为；一切都依最精确完善的准则进行。
quotes.textEnglish: Let nothing be done rashly, and at random, but all things according to the most exact and perfect rules of art.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Let opinion be taken away, and no man will think himself wronged.
quotes.textChinese: 除去主观判断，就不会觉得自己受了委屈。
quotes.textEnglish: Let opinion be taken away, and no man will think himself wronged.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: If thou shalt find anything in this mortal life better than righteousness,
quotes.textChinese: 若你能在世上找到比正义更好的事物……
quotes.textEnglish: If thou shalt find anything in this mortal life better than righteousness,

quotes.sourceExcerpt: The best kind of revenge is, not to become like unto them.
quotes.textChinese: 最好的报复，就是不要变得和他们一样。
quotes.textEnglish: The best kind of revenge is, not to become like unto them.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: According to the nature of the universe all things particular are determined.
quotes.textChinese: 宇宙中的每一件事，都依其整体本性而有定序。
quotes.textEnglish: According to the nature of the universe all things particular are determined.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Hast thou reason? I have. Why then makest thou not use of it?
quotes.textChinese: 你有理性吗？有。那为什么不运用它呢？
quotes.textEnglish: Hast thou reason? I have. Why then makest thou not use of it?

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
quotes.textChinese: 有些事由我们掌握，有些事不由我们掌握。
quotes.textEnglish: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Remember that desire contains in it the profession (hope) of obtaining
quotes.textChinese: 要记得，欲望总带着「我能得到所求」的预期。
quotes.textEnglish: Remember that desire contains in it the profession (hope) of obtaining

quotes.sourceExcerpt: When you are going to take in hand any act remind yourself what kind of an act it is.
quotes.textChinese: 开始做一件事之前，先提醒自己那会是怎样的过程。
quotes.textEnglish: When you are going to take in hand any act remind yourself what kind of an act it is.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
quotes.textChinese: 使人困扰的不是事情本身，而是人对事情的看法。
quotes.textEnglish: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Seek not that the things which happen should happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are.
quotes.textChinese: 不要要求事情照你的愿望发生；试着愿意事情如其所是。
quotes.textEnglish: Seek not that the things which happen should happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Disease is an impediment to the body, but not to the will, unless the will itself chooses.
quotes.textChinese: 疾病阻碍身体，却不必然阻碍意志，除非意志自己选择屈服。
quotes.textEnglish: Disease is an impediment to the body, but not to the will, unless the will itself chooses.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: On the occasion of every accident (event) that befalls you, remember to turn to yourself and inquire what power you have for turning it to use.
quotes.textChinese: 每逢意外，回到自己身上，看看能用什么力量把它转为助益。
quotes.textEnglish: On the occasion of every accident (event) that befalls you, remember to turn to yourself and inquire what power you have for turning it to use.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Never say about anything, I have lost it, but say I have restored it.
quotes.textChinese: 不要说「我失去了」，而要说「我已归还」。
quotes.textEnglish: Never say about anything, I have lost it, but say I have restored it.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: If you would improve, submit to be considered without sense and foolish with respect to externals.
quotes.textChinese: 想要进步，就甘愿在外物上被人看作不明事理。
quotes.textEnglish: If you would improve, submit to be considered without sense and foolish with respect to externals.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: If you would have your children and your wife and your friends to live for ever, you are silly;
quotes.textChinese: 若你希望孩子、伴侣和朋友永远不变，那是不切实际的。
quotes.textEnglish: If you would have your children and your wife and your friends to live for ever, you are silly;

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Remember that in life you ought to behave as at a banquet.
quotes.textChinese: 人生如宴席，合宜地接受眼前所至之物。
quotes.textEnglish: Remember that in life you ought to behave as at a banquet.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Remember that thou art an actor in a play, of such a kind as the teacher (author) may choose;
quotes.textChinese: 记住，你是剧中演员，角色由作者安排。
quotes.textEnglish: Remember that thou art an actor in a play, of such a kind as the teacher (author) may choose;

quotes.sourceExcerpt: When a raven has croaked inauspiciously, let not the appearance hurry you away with it;
quotes.textChinese: 乌鸦叫得不吉利时，不要被表象牵着走。
quotes.textEnglish: When a raven has croaked inauspiciously, let not the appearance hurry you away with it;

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Let death and exile and every other thing which appears dreadful be daily before your eyes;
quotes.textChinese: 把死亡、流放以及其他看似可怕的事放在眼前思量。
quotes.textEnglish: Let death and exile and every other thing which appears dreadful be daily before your eyes;

quotes.sourceExcerpt: In every act observe the things which come first, and those which follow it; and so proceed to the act.
quotes.textChinese: 每个行动前先看清它的前因与后果，再决定是否开始。
quotes.textEnglish: In every act observe the things which come first, and those which follow it; and so proceed to the act.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: STUDIES serve for delight, for ornament, and for ability.
quotes.textChinese: 读书使人愉悦，增添文采，也增长才干。
quotes.textEnglish: STUDIES serve for delight, for ornament, and for ability.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Reading maketh a full man; conference a ready man; and writing an exact man.
quotes.textChinese: 阅读使人充实，交谈使人敏捷，写作使人严谨。
quotes.textEnglish: Reading maketh a full man; conference a ready man; and writing an exact man.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Histories make men wise; poets witty; the mathematics subtile; natural philosophy deep; moral grave; logic and rhetoric able to contend.
quotes.textChinese: 历史使人明智，诗使人灵巧，数学使人精密，自然哲学使人深刻。
quotes.textEnglish: Histories make men wise; poets witty; the mathematics subtile; natural philosophy deep; moral grave; logic and rhetoric able to contend.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Some books are to be tasted, others to be swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested.
quotes.textChinese: 有些书浅尝即可，有些可以整本读下，有少数要细嚼慢咽。
quotes.textEnglish: Some books are to be tasted, others to be swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Crafty men contemn studies, simple men admire them, and wise men use them.
quotes.textChinese: 狡黠者轻视学问，浅薄者仰慕学问，明智者运用学问。
quotes.textEnglish: Crafty men contemn studies, simple men admire them, and wise men use them.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: To spend too much time in studies is sloth.
quotes.textChinese: 读书耗时过多，是怠惰。
quotes.textEnglish: To spend too much time in studies is sloth.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: To use them too much for ornament, is affectation.
quotes.textChinese: 把学问过度用来装点门面，是矫饰。
quotes.textEnglish: To use them too much for ornament, is affectation.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: To make judgment wholly by their rules, is the humor of a scholar.
quotes.textChinese: 全凭书本规则作判断，是学究气。
quotes.textEnglish: To make judgment wholly by their rules, is the humor of a scholar.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Studies themselves do give forth directions too much at large, except they be bounded in by experience.
quotes.textChinese: 学问给出的指引往往宽泛，须由经验加以界定。
quotes.textEnglish: Studies themselves do give forth directions too much at large, except they be bounded in by experience.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: For natural abilities are like natural plants, that need proyning by study.
quotes.textChinese: 天赋如天然生长的植物，需要学习修剪。
quotes.textEnglish: For natural abilities are like natural plants, that need proyning by study.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: Truth may perhaps come to the price of a pearl, that showeth best by day.
quotes.textChinese: 真理或许如珍珠，最适合在日光下显现。
quotes.textEnglish: Truth may perhaps come to the price of a pearl, that showeth best by day.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: A mixture of a lie doth ever add pleasure.
quotes.textChinese: 掺入谎言，总会添几分诱惑。
quotes.textEnglish: A mixture of a lie doth ever add pleasure.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: There is surely no greater wisdom, than well to time the beginnings, and onsets, of things.
quotes.textChinese: 没有什么比把握事情开始的时机更需要智慧。
quotes.textEnglish: There is surely no greater wisdom, than well to time the beginnings, and onsets, of things.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: He that will not apply new remedies, must expect new evils; for time is the greatest innovator.
quotes.textChinese: 不肯采用新疗法的人，必须面对新的弊病；时间本身就是最大的革新者。
quotes.textEnglish: He that will not apply new remedies, must expect new evils; for time is the greatest innovator.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: There is no excellent beauty, that hath not some strangeness in the proportion.
quotes.textChinese: 真正出众的美，总带着某种不寻常的比例。
quotes.textEnglish: There is no excellent beauty, that hath not some strangeness in the proportion.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: To be, or not to be: that is the question:
quotes.textChinese: 生存还是毁灭，这是问题。
quotes.textEnglish: To be, or not to be: that is the question:

quotes.locator: Julius Caesar, Act I, Scene II
quotes.sourceExcerpt: The fault, deere Brutus, is not in our Starres, But in our Selues.
quotes.textChinese: 亲爱的布鲁图斯，错不在星辰，而在我们自己。
quotes.textEnglish: The fault, deere Brutus, is not in our Starres, But in our Selues.

quotes.locator: Measure for Measure, Act I, Scene IV
quotes.sourceExcerpt: Our doubts are traitors And makes vs loose the good we oft might win, By fearing to attempt:
quotes.textChinese: 疑虑会背叛我们，使我们因害怕尝试而失去本可得到的好结果。
quotes.textEnglish: Our doubts are traitors And makes vs loose the good we oft might win, By fearing to attempt:

quotes.locator: As You Like It, Act II, Scene VII
quotes.sourceExcerpt: All the worlds a stage, And all the men and women meerely Players.
quotes.textChinese: 整个世界是一座舞台，男男女女不过是演员。
quotes.textEnglish: All the worlds a stage, And all the men and women meerely Players.

quotes.locator: King Lear, Act I, Scene I
quotes.sourceExcerpt: Nothing will come of nothing.
quotes.textChinese: 一无所出，源于一无所为。
quotes.textEnglish: Nothing will come of nothing.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.
quotes.textChinese: 世上没有绝对的好与坏，是思想使它如此。
quotes.textEnglish: There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.

quotes.locator: The Merchant of Venice, Act V, Scene I
quotes.sourceExcerpt: How farre that little candell throwes his beames, So shines a good deed in a naughty world
quotes.textChinese: 小小烛光照得多远！善行在混浊世间也是如此闪耀。
quotes.textEnglish: How farre that little candell throwes his beames, So shines a good deed in a naughty world

quotes.locator: Twelfth Night, Act II, Scene V
quotes.sourceExcerpt: Why some are borne great, some atchieue greatnesse, and some haue greatnesse throwne vpon them.
quotes.textChinese: 有人生而显赫，有人成就卓越，也有人被命运推上高位。
quotes.textEnglish: Why some are borne great, some atchieue greatnesse, and some haue greatnesse throwne vpon them.

quotes.locator: All’s Well That Ends Well, Act I, Scene I
quotes.sourceExcerpt: Our remedies oft in our selues do lye, Which we ascribe to heauen.
quotes.textChinese: 我们常把疗方归于上天，其实它往往就在自己身上。
quotes.textEnglish: Our remedies oft in our selues do lye, Which we ascribe to heauen.

quotes.locator: The Tempest, Act II, Scene I
quotes.sourceExcerpt: Whereof, what's past is Prologue;
quotes.textChinese: 过去只是序幕。
quotes.textEnglish: Whereof, what's past is Prologue;

quotes.locator: Julius Caesar, Act I, Scene II
quotes.sourceExcerpt: Men at sometime, are Masters of their Fates.
quotes.textChinese: 人有时能掌握自己的命运。
quotes.textEnglish: Men at sometime, are Masters of their Fates.

quotes.sourceExcerpt: This aboue all; to thine owne selfe be true.
quotes.textChinese: 最重要的是，对自己真诚。
quotes.textEnglish: This aboue all; to thine owne selfe be true.

quotes.locator: King Lear, Act I, Scene IV
quotes.sourceExcerpt: Haue more then thou showest, Speake lesse then thou knowest,
quotes.textChinese: 拥有胜于显露，少说胜于多知。
quotes.textEnglish: Haue more then thou showest, Speake lesse then thou knowest,

quotes.locator: The Merchant of Venice, Act II, Scene VII
quotes.sourceExcerpt: All that glisters is not gold.
quotes.textChinese: 闪闪发光的未必都是金子。
quotes.textEnglish: All that glisters is not gold.
